licence.title: Data & licences
licence.intro: Vestigia is built on data that others made freely reusable. Terms differ by layer — here is what applies to each.
licence.recordsBody: Site and tracing text is CC BY-SA — free to reuse and adapt, including commercially, provided changes are shared under the same licence and the source is credited. The structured metadata (coordinates, dates, categories) is CC0 — no rights reserved.
licence.imagesBody: Every photograph carries its own licence and attribution, shown beneath the image itself. Licences vary per record; check the image before reusing it separately from the site it illustrates.
licence.barringtonBody: Ancient coastline, roads, water and places are drawn from the Ancient World Mapping Center (ODbL 1.0) and Pleiades (CC BY 3.0). Both are reusable, including commercially, with attribution — ODbL's share-alike applies to the underlying database, not to the rendered map tiles.
licence.dareBody: This basemap is CC BY-SA 3.0 from Johan Åhlfeldt (Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire, Gothenburg University) — but two of its own source layers are credited non-commercial (CC BY-NC 3.0 / CC BY-NC-SA), which the blanket CC BY-SA cannot override. Treat this specific layer as non-commercial use only.
licence.limesBody: The frontier line is derived from the Ancient World Mapping Center's extent of the empire (ODbL 1.0) and is not part of the contributed database.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page states what Vestigia collects, why, for how long, and who else sees it — plainly, and matching what the code actually does rather than a generic template. It is not a substitute for reading the source, which is open.
privacy.controllerBody: The service provider named in the legal notice is the controller ("we") for the processing described below. Contact details are the same as on that page.
privacy.accountBody: Registering stores your email address, display name and a salted password hash (argon2id — the password itself is never stored). This is processed to perform the contract of providing an account (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)). Your address is used only to verify it, to let you sign in and reset a forgotten password, and to tell you about decisions on your own contributions or account — never for marketing, and there is no newsletter.
privacy.contributionBody: A site, tracing or image you submit is linked to your account so the edit history stays legible and so trust can be evaluated. Approved contributions are public, as is the fact that your account made them — this is how the atlas's revision history works, and it is core to what the service is. If you delete your account, this link is anonymised (see "Your rights" below) rather than the contribution being removed, for the reasons stated there.
privacy.photographBody: Every uploaded image is re-encoded on our server before storage, which strips EXIF metadata — including any embedded GPS coordinates or camera/device identifiers — so none of that reaches storage or another visitor.
privacy.cookiesBody: Three cookies, all strictly necessary for functionality you directly requested, none used for tracking or advertising: a session cookie (kept 7 days, or until you sign out) that keeps you signed in; a cookie that remembers your light/dark preference; and a cookie that remembers your chosen interface language. Because none of them is optional, none of them can be tracking, and none of them supports advertising, German law (§25(2) TDDDG, implementing the ePrivacy Directive) does not require asking for consent before setting them — so there is no cookie banner here. This section is that disclosure.
privacy.logsBody: Every request is logged with the visitor's IP address, kept for 30 days, on the legitimate-interest basis of operating and securing the service (Art. 6(1)(f)) — investigating abuse, debugging failures, and defending against automated attacks. Passwords, email addresses and authentication tokens are never written to logs. Rate-limiting briefly stores your IP address (at most one hour) to enforce fair-use limits and stop automated signup and scraping.
privacy.recipientsHeading: Who else processes data, and where
privacy.recipientsIntro: The following process data on our behalf or receive it as part of operating the service. None of them may use it for their own purposes.
privacy.recipientHosting: Hosting: the application and database run on a server in the EU.
privacy.recipientCdn: CDN and object storage (Bunny.net): serves images and map tiles; terminates encrypted connections inside the EU.
privacy.recipientMail: Transactional email (Lettermint, Amsterdam): sends account and moderation emails — verification links, password resets, decisions on your contributions.
privacy.recipientTranslate: Machine translation (LibreTranslate): runs on our own server, not a third party — borrowed article text is translated there, never sent externally.
privacy.recipientEnrichment: Wikidata, Wikipedia and Pleiades (outside the EU): when a site's description can be supplemented from these public projects, our server — never your browser — makes that request, so your IP address is not shared with them.
privacy.recipientBasemap: Map tile providers: some basemap layers are fetched directly by your browser from their own hosts, so your IP address reaches them the way it would visiting any site that embeds a map.
privacy.recipientSecurity: Automated abuse detection (CrowdSec): IP addresses our server locally flags as abusive are shared with CrowdSec's community threat-intelligence service, on the legitimate-interest basis of network security (Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacy.rightsBody: You can request a copy of what we hold about your account and its contributions, and you can delete your account, both from within the app once signed in — export returns everything as a file you can keep; deletion removes your email address and display name and cannot be undone. Deleting your account does not remove your approved contributions from the atlas — those remain, attributed to a removed account rather than to you, on the basis that the historical record of what was recorded and when is itself information of public and scientific interest (Art. 17(3)(d)) and consistent with how any other edit's history is kept. You can also ask us directly for rectification, restriction of processing, or to object to processing based on legitimate interest, and you have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority.
